subject: Cost parity conversation and proposed tier restructure
messages:
From: Sarah Blake <sarah@datagore.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@dataforge.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Cost comparison + ask: can Redwood bridge to OpenAI parity for hosted API?

Hi Olga,

Quick intro — I'm Sarah on the infrastructure team at DataForge Labs. We ran a 3-week eval of several hosted inference providers for our analytics assistant (US region), and our cost model shows OpenAI's per-token economics are ~28-35% cheaper than Redwood at our current run-rate (roughly 25B tokens / month, peak concurrency in the 100s).

Attached is a short benchmark and a calc sheet showing expected monthly spend (dataforge_benchmark_oct16.pdf). Before we recommend a migration, we wanted to ask: is there room to restructure committed tiers or offer a temporary competitor bridge so we can keep latency/feature parity while you help close the pricing gap?

Key asks:
- Indicative per-token rates if we commit to a 6–12 month tier (25B+/mo).
- Any one-time transition or displacement credits you would consider for customers moving from a competitor.
- Clarify how egress/region pricing would apply for cross-region fallbacks.

We like Redwood's serving guarantees and the observability surface — it would be preferable to avoid re-architecting. Can we set a short call next week to go over numbers?

Thanks,
Sarah Blake
DataForge Labs — Infrastructure
Attachments: dataforge_benchmark_oct16.pdf (pdf, 432KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah@datagore.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost comparison + ask: can Redwood bridge to OpenAI parity for hosted API?

Sarah — thanks for the note and for sharing the benchmark. I pulled this into Marcus and Neha to align on options. We absolutely want to keep DataForge on Redwood if we can close the economics gap.

Quick propose: Marcus will send a concrete tiered proposal (per-token bands + commit levels) and a short displacement-credit construct for a transitional period. Can you share the cadence you expect (6 vs 12 months) and whether the 25B token figure is sustained or a projected peak? That helps us size the discounts.

I can make time Thursday or Friday for a 30-min call. Suggested times: Thu 10/22 11:00am PT or Fri 10/23 9:30am PT.

Best,
Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Blake <sarah@datagore.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost comparison + ask: can Redwood bridge to OpenAI parity for hosted API? — proposal attached

Sarah — thanks for the benchmark. We reviewed usage shape with Product and Finance; based on the 25B tokens/month baseline you provided, here's an actionable structure we can offer:

Summary (high level)
- Term options: 6-month or 12-month committed tiers.
- Tiered per-token rates (USD, per 1k tokens):
  * 0–5B: $0.045
  * 5–20B: $0.032
  * 20B+: $0.024
- For a 12-month commit at your 25B baseline we would apply an additional sustained-usage discount that brings the blended per-token to ~ $0.026 — this maps within ~10% of the numbers you cited for competitive parity.

Displacement bridge (one-time, limited)
- We will provide a transition credit equal to 10% of your first-month invoiced usage (applied as a bill credit) if you sign a 12-month commit within 30 days. This is a limited program (one-time per account) intended to help offset migration friction.

Operational notes
- Egress and cross-region fallbacks: standard cloud egress charges apply. For multi-region redundancy we can either route to the closest Redwood region (no additional per-token premium) or route to a warm failover with negotiated egress pass-through — details in the attached sheet.
- SLA: 99.9% availability target for committed capacity with credits for missed SLOs; we can surface specific obligations in the contract addendum.

I attached a detailed tier spreadsheet and a short walk-through (redwood_restructured_tiers_q4_v3.xlsx). If that looks reasonable we can draft a short amendment and loop Legal/Procurement.

I copied Neha from Finance to confirm billing cadence and to help expedite contract review. If you want to take the 12-month path we can fast-track a DocuSign with the displacement credit language.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_restructured_tiers_q4_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)
From: Sarah Blake <sarah@datagore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@dataforge.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost comparison + ask: can Redwood bridge to OpenAI parity for hosted API? — DataForge response

Marcus / Olga — appreciate the fast follow. The proposed bands and the 10% first-month credit look promising. A few clarifications before we move to contract:

1) Blended example: can you provide a sample invoice estimate for month 1 and month 3 under the 12-month commit (showing how the blended $0.026 ~ will appear)?
2) SLA: we need the uptime credit formula in writing and a customer-facing MTTI/MTTR playbook for committed capacity.
3) Egress: we prefer that Redwood absorb cross-region egress costs for failover traffic up to a modest cap (we can propose $5k/mo). If that requires a small add-on to the commit we can consider it.

Procurement has also attached a draft PO for internal routing (dataforge_po_1021.pdf). We run a small set of safety checks on Anthropic for sensitive prompts; that doesn’t change the primary traffic split but worth a note.

If you can return the invoice examples and a one-paragraph SLA addendum, we can move to signatures next week.

Thanks — Sarah
Attachments: dataforge_po_1021.pdf (pdf, 56KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: quick approval request — DataForge 12m commit with displacement credit

Team — DataForge is ready to proceed pending: 1) an invoice example for months 1 and 3 (Marcus), 2) a one-paragraph SLA addendum we can attach to the amendment (Legal), and 3) confirmation from Finance that the 10% first-month credit can be handled as a bill credit against the first invoice (Neha).

Key commercial ask: 12-month commit at the tiering Marcus proposed + 10% displacement credit (one-time). They also requested Redwood absorb up to $5k/mo of cross-region egress for failover traffic — we should decide if that is a flat add-on to the commit or covered under standard terms.

Please confirm by end of day so we can issue the DocuSign to DataForge and close before month-end.

Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
(Internal only)
